rule: Affect is usually a verb: to change or influence something. Effect is usually a noun: the result of a change.
trick: Affect is the Action; Effect is the End result.

qs.s: The heat will ___ the wheat crop in Punjab.
The new metro line has had a big ___ on traffic in Pune.
Loud wedding music late at night can ___ a baby's sleep.

rule: Advice is a noun: the help or opinion you give. Advise is a verb: the act of giving it.
trick: You give advICE like a thing; you adviSe as an action.

qs.s: My nani's ___ is to save a little every month.
Doctors ___ drinking plenty of water during a Chennai summer.
Can you give me some ___ about choosing a college in Delhi?

rule: Lose (one o) is a verb: to fail to keep, find or win something. Loose (two o's) is an adjective: not tight.
trick: Lose has lost an o.

qs.s: Don't ___ your metro card on the way to Rajiv Chowk.
This kurta is too ___; I need a smaller size.
If we drop one more catch, we will ___ the match.

rule: You lend something to someone: you give it for a while. You borrow something from someone: you take it for a while.
trick: Lend goes out; borrow comes in.

qs.s: Meena, could you ___ me your scooter for an hour?
Can I ___ your notes from yesterday's chemistry class?
Arjun had to ___ ₹500 from his roommate to pay the electricity bill.

rule: Use fewer for things you can count (fewer buses). Use less for things you cannot count (less water, less noise).
trick: Can you count it? Fewer. Can you only measure it? Less.

qs.s: There were ___ passengers on the Mumbai local because of the holiday.
Please put ___ sugar in my chai.
This year, ___ students failed the maths board exam.

rule: Economic means to do with the economy, trade or money. Economical means saving money or not wasting things.
trick: Economic is about the economy; economical is about your wallet.

qs.s: The budget speech focused on ___ growth.
A small hatchback is more ___ than an SUV for city driving.
Farmers in Vidarbha face serious ___ problems when the rains fail.

rule: Sensible means having good judgement; practical. Sensitive means easily affected or hurt, or quick to notice others' feelings.
trick: Sensible people are wise; sensitive teeth hurt.

qs.s: Wearing a helmet on a bike is the ___ thing to do.
My teeth are ___ to cold water.
Carrying an umbrella in the Kerala monsoon is a ___ plan.

rule: Principal is the head of a school, or means 'main'. Principle is a basic rule or belief.
trick: The principal is your pal; a principle is a rule.

qs.s: The ___ called a meeting of all class teachers.
My grandfather never told lies; it was a matter of ___ for him.
Rice is the ___ crop of West Bengal.

rule: Stationary means not moving. Stationery means paper, pens, envelopes and other writing things.
trick: Stationery has e for envelope; stationary has a for 'at rest'.

qs.s: The bus was ___ at the signal when the auto hit it.
Riya bought notebooks and pens from the ___ shop near her school.
Keep the bike ___ while the attendant fills petrol.

rule: A compliment is praise. A complement is something that goes well with another thing or makes it complete.
trick: I like compliments; a complement completes.

qs.s: Aunty paid me a ___ on my Bengali.
Coconut chutney is the perfect ___ to a crisp dosa.
The interviewer's ___ about my project made me smile.

rule: It's is short for 'it is' or 'it has'. Its means 'belonging to it' and has no apostrophe, like his and her.
trick: If 'it is' fits, write it's.

qs.s: I think ___ going to rain in Mumbai today.
The cat licked ___ paw on the verandah.
The bank changed ___ logo last year.

rule: Than is for comparing (taller than). Then is about time or order (first this, then that).
trick: thAn compAres; thEn is about whEn.

qs.s: Kolkata is more humid ___ Delhi in August.
Finish your homework, and ___ you can watch the match.
My brother is two years older ___ me.

rule: In British and Indian English, practice is the noun and practise is the verb. American English uses practice for both.
trick: Same pattern as advice (noun) and advise (verb).

qs.s: You must ___ every day if you want to sing ragas well.
Cricket ___ starts at six in the morning.
Dr Fernandes runs a busy medical ___ in Panaji.

rule: Accept is a verb: to take or agree to something. Except means 'but not' or 'leaving out'.
trick: EXcept EXcludes.

qs.s: Please ___ this small gift from our family.
Everyone came to the wedding ___ my uncle from Dubai.
Most shops in our market ___ UPI payments now.

rule: Adapt means to change to suit a new situation. Adopt means to take something or someone as your own.
trick: Adapt to fit; adopt an option.

qs.s: It took Anjali a month to ___ to the Delhi winter.
The couple decided to ___ a baby girl.
My cousin wants to ___ a stray puppy from our lane.

rule: Beside means next to. Besides means 'in addition to' or 'also'.
trick: Beside is by the side; besides adds something extra.

qs.s: Come and sit ___ me on the bench.
What else do you eat for breakfast ___ idli?
The old temple stands ___ the river.

rule: Ensure means to make sure something happens. Insure means to buy insurance against loss or damage.
trick: Insure involves insurance.

qs.s: Please ___ that the gas is switched off before you leave.
It is wise to ___ your new car before you drive it.
The headmistress will ___ that every child gets a mid-day meal.

rule: The speaker implies: hints at something without saying it. The listener infers: works it out from the hints.
trick: Imply goes out from the speaker; infer comes in to the listener.

qs.s: Are you trying to ___ that I ate the last laddoo?
From the dark clouds over Guwahati, we can ___ that it will rain.
Her silence seemed to ___ that she disliked the plan.

rule: Historic means important enough to be remembered in history. Historical means about, or from, the past.
trick: Historic makes history; historical is about history.

qs.s: India's ___ moon landing made headlines around the world.
The museum in Hyderabad has many ___ documents from the Nizam's time.
The ___ novel is set in Mughal Delhi.

rule: Continual means happening again and again, with breaks. Continuous means going on without any break.
trick: Continuous is one unbroken line; continual keeps coming back.

qs.s: It rained for 48 hours, a ___ downpour with no break at all.
These ___ phone calls, one after another, stop me from working.
A ___ white line in the middle of the road means you must not overtake.

rule: Eminent means famous and respected. Imminent means about to happen very soon.
trick: Imminent is coming in a minute.

qs.s: An ___ scientist from IISc gave the lecture.
Fishermen were warned that a cyclone was ___.
The ___ singer was honoured with a Padma award.

rule: Discreet means careful not to embarrass people or give away secrets. Discrete means separate and distinct.
trick: In discrete, the t keeps the two e's separate.

qs.s: Please be ___ about the surprise party for Dadi.
The course is divided into four ___ modules.
A good bank manager is always ___ about customers' money.

rule: Everyday (one word) describes a noun: ordinary, normal. Every day (two words) means each day.
trick: If you can say "each day", write two words.

qs.s: Traffic jams are an ___ problem in Bengaluru.
Nani walks in the park ___ at six.
Wear your ___ clothes; it is not a wedding.

rule: A council is a group of people who meet to decide things. Counsel is advice, a lawyer, or the act of advising.
trick: A council is a committee; counsel is consulting.

qs.s: The municipal ___ voted to build a new park in Indore.
The senior ___ argued the case in the Supreme Court.
Schools should ___ students who feel stressed before exams.

rule: Emigrate means to leave your country to live in another. Immigrate means to come into a new country to live.
trick: Emigrate is Exit; Immigrate is In.

qs.s: My uncle wants to ___ from India next year.
Canada allows many skilled workers to ___ into the country each year.
In 1972, many Gujarati families had to ___ from Uganda.

rule: Elicit is a verb: to draw out an answer or reaction. Illicit is an adjective: illegal or not allowed.
trick: Illicit is illegal; both start with ill.

qs.s: The teacher asked simple questions to ___ answers from shy students.
Police seized a truck carrying ___ liquor.
The quiz host's joke failed to ___ a single laugh.
